title: Cloudy apple juice 1L glass bottles (fill-cap-label)

product.name: 1L cloudy apple juice bottle
product.description: Cloudy apple juice bottled into 1 litre glass bottles with a red screw cap and a paper label. Bottle size is about 90 mm diameter and 260 mm tall (≈1L volume).

steps.name: Fill
steps.does: Fill the sanitized empty glass bottle with cloudy apple juice through a nozzle (~6 seconds filling).

steps.name: Cap
steps.does: Screw on the red cap to the filled bottle (~3 seconds).

steps.name: Label
steps.does: Apply the paper label to the capped bottle (~2 seconds).

steps.name: Inspect
steps.does: Use a camera to check fill level, cap presence/condition, and label placement.

steps.name: DivertRejects
steps.does: Reject any bad bottles by diverting them off the line at the inspection station (single-lane divert).

quality: Camera inspection finds bad bottles (fill level, cap, or label issues); those units are diverted off-line at the inspection station.
constraints: One bottle at a time on a belt
Inspection + reject must happen as a single-lane divert at the inspection station
Food-contact equipment kept sanitary (owner: bottles arrive sanitized and rinsed)
assumptions: Bottles arrive already sanitized and rinsed, empty, with caps supplied separately to the line (no bottle-wash/sanitization on this line).
Cap feed is available to the capping station (e.g., magazine/bowl feeder) and capping can apply the red screw cap reliably at the stated cycle time.
Label application is a single label per bottle, applied consistently within the stated ~2 seconds.
“About 6 seconds of filling” refers to the fill operation time budget only; pre/post nozzle movements are handled within each station’s takt budget.
The target of 240 bottles/hour is achievable with one-bottle-per-indexing on the belt; line takt is 15.0 s per bottle (derived from 240/h).
